items.explanation: 80-year-old woman (DOB 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 2025-09-12 through 2026-05-28. Current medications as of 2026-09-24 are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg only (orders 6c299df3-9a95-5df0-bd21-7812b0f6f4a8, 73203e4f-64f2-5940-a625-b77869a71435); no oral anticoagulant order is active and none is documented in any note. CHA2DS2-VASc 9: CHF (I110 hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, I509, I5043), hypertension (I10/4019), age >=75 (2), diabetes (E119/E11649), prior stroke/TIA (2; V1254 personal history of TIA/cerebral infarction, I69322/I69351 sequelae of cerebral infarction), vascular disease (old MI 412, coronary atherosclerosis I2510/41400), female sex. Guideline-recommended anticoagulation is absent - needs prescriber review.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) has been prescribed since 2022-03-01; the current order c6f532e9 (2026-08-22, valid to 2027-01-05) is active at 2026-09-24, together with warfarin and metoprolol succinate. This 95-year-old patient on amiodarone plus a beta blocker with a QTc of 539 ms requires prescriber review per the QT monitoring memo of 2025-01-15; no ECG has been repeated since 2022.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation (Condition 42731, encounter 2025-08-22) carried in the cardiology clinic problem list in all notes from 2025-10-10 to 2026-07-28. 71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (Condition I480, 2025-03-14 admission) diagnosed during the same admission as an embolic cerebral infarction (I6340/I639). Active outpatient orders at 2026-09-24 are carvedilol 6.25 mg, metoprolol tartrate 25 mg and famotidine 20 mg (7e0c38f4-4f79-5e98-99b7-3cd87ca7e996, e0caf017-f9d9-5a9b-a138-92d7ddf91cc6, d897c346-e671-5f45-a8c7-e8a7cbb10a4b) - rate control only, with no anticoagulant. Anticoagulation is strongly indicated after a cardioembolic stroke with AF; documented thrombocytopenia (D696) and history of falling (Z9181) are relevant to the risk discussion but no decision is recorded. Needs prescriber review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic visit (order dc397aff, valid 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28, active at 2026-09-24) despite the outside-records summary of 2026-08-12, which documents an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and states that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. The 2026-08-20 note simply lists apixaban as a current medication and says 'continue current regimen'; no review of the bleeding event or a decision to resume is documented, and concomitant aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg were also continued. Anticoagulant continuation after a major GI bleed needs prescriber review.

Two direct oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active. At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started (order 7206d5b5, valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) for the stated purpose of switching from rivaroxaban, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same visit (order b71a461f, valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25) and the visit note lists both drugs on the current medication list. Both orders remain in force at 2026-09-24 and neither has been stopped, so the patient (paroxysmal AF/flutter, CLL) is exposed to duplicate full-dose anticoagulation. Needs immediate clarification of which agent is intended.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no organised P waves (RR 0.30-0.60 s, RR coefficient of variation 0.16-0.19) at a mean rate of 140-144/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - not sinus rhythm at 72. Unspecified atrial fibrillation (Condition 54ec94da-144c-5ec2-a135-76f7a52d00ac) was also coded at the 2026-06-10 18:36 encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the chart needs correction and the rate/rhythm reassessed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) has been continuously prescribed since 2024-05-14 and the current order 8de890c6 (2026-04-23, valid to 2027-01-02) is active at 2026-09-24. The most recent ECG in the chart, 108018814 of 2023-10-08, is sinus rhythm at 68/min with a markedly prolonged repolarisation: QRS 84 ms, QT 481 ms, RR 880 ms, giving Bazett QTc 513 ms (>=500 ms). The 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this tracing as 'QT acceptable', which is not supported by the measurements. Most recent electrolytes (2025-08-23) are normal: potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, so QTc prolongation is not explained by electrolyte depletion. Per the QT monitoring memo of 2025-01-15 this requires prescriber review.

The most recent ECG, 106885519 of 2025-11-24 (obtained 14 days after amiodarone was started), shows sinus rhythm at 62/min, PR 170 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 513 ms with RR 968 ms, giving Bazett QTc 522 ms (>=500 ms). This is a marked increase from the pre-amiodarone tracing 108780865 of 2025-06-07 (QTc 409 ms). Most recent electrolytes (2026-04-20) are normal: potassium 4.4 mEq/L, magnesium 2.2 mg/dL. Requires prescriber review per the QT monitoring memo of 2025-01-15.

Requires prescriber review per the QT monitoring memo of 2025-01-15.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm, 81/min (RR 0.66-0.86 s, gradual respiratory variation), upright consistent P in II/aVF (0.22 mV) and biphasic in V1, P axis about +74. PR 190 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 326 ms with RR 744 ms -> Bazett QTc 378 ms. Frontal QRS axis +48 (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Despite a history of atrial fibrillation and citalopram/apixaban therapy, this tracing is in sinus rhythm, consistent with the 2026-03-07 note. No previous ECG in the chart, so no comparison possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 104/min, regular, with large upright P waves in I/II (0.22 mV, P axis about +48) and a deep negative P component in V1; PR about 150 ms, QRS 92 ms. QT 358 ms with RR 579 ms -> QTc 470 ms. Frontal axis +39 (normal); no bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-06-20 also showed sinus rhythm but at 147/min, where the T wave merges with the following P wave so the QT cannot be measured reliably (estimates range from about 275 to 360 ms, QTc 430-565 ms); no confident QTc change of 60 ms or more can be asserted, and rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia, 109/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.03), with upright P waves in I and II; PR about 145 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 346 ms with RR 548 ms -> QTc 467 ms (mildly prolonged; Bazett over-corrects at this rate). Frontal QRS axis +36 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 144/min. RR intervals range 0.30-0.60 s (coefficient of variation 0.16, normalised RMSSD 0.22) with only 57% of cycles within 10% of the median, and there is no organised P wave - the deflection preceding the QRS is negative in I and II and not reproducible, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 90 ms, QT 291 ms with RR 416 ms -> QTc 452 ms. Frontal axis +3 (normal); no bundle branch block. The previous ECG, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same evening (107914094), also showed atrial fibrillation at 140/min with QRS 90 ms and QTc 444 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of the same morning recorded 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 0.864-0.882 s) with a small, reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS that is positive in lead I (+0.07 mV) but negative in II and aVF (-0.04 and -0.07 mV) and biphasic in V1, giving a P axis of about -45. This inverted inferior P axis with a fixed PR indicates a low atrial/ectopic atrial (non-sinus) rhythm rather than sinus rhythm, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER. PR 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 396 ms with RR 873 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis -24 (normal). No bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-04-27 also showed a regular 60/min rhythm with negative P waves in II (QTc 397 ms) but with a globally inverted lead I suggesting arm-lead reversal; there is no change in rhythm category, bundle branch block or QTc (difference 27 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.02), with upright P waves in II/aVF (0.18 mV, P axis about +76); PR about 125 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT 306 ms with RR 616 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +6 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with a small upright P wave in II and a biphasic P in V1; PR about 140 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 373 ms with RR 832 ms -> QTc 409 ms. Frontal QRS axis +20 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; note this remains the most recent tracing despite escitalopram having been started on 2026-08-01.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean 53/min. RR intervals range 0.78-1.60 s (coefficient of variation 0.20, normalised RMSSD 0.29) with only 56% of cycles within 10% of the median, and the TP/PR segments are flat in lead II with no identifiable P wave, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 88 ms, QT 425 ms with RR 1128 ms -> QTc 400 ms. Frontal QRS axis +3 (normal); deep V1/V2 S waves but no bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2024-11-12 (107873952) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with a clear 0.22 mV P wave in II, PR 190 ms, QRS 78 ms and QTc 396 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new on this tracing; the QTc is unchanged (difference 4 ms).

Sinus bradycardia, 58/min, regular, with upright P waves in II (0.16 mV, P axis about +75); PR about 120 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 421 ms with RR 1030 ms -> QTc 414 ms. Frontal QRS axis +62 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2025-03-08 (sinus 62/min, PR about 116 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 437 ms, axis +61) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 23 ms). This remains the most recent tracing although haloperidol was started on 2026-09-15.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), with upright P waves in I/II/aVF; PR about 155 ms, QRS 64 ms, QT 337 ms with RR 720 ms -> QTc 397 ms. Frontal QRS axis +52 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 77/min, regular, with prominent upright P waves in II (0.27 mV, P axis about +76); PR about 160 ms, QRS 62 ms, QT 402 ms with RR 783 ms -> QTc 454 ms. Frontal QRS axis +63 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2020-02-02 (109048192) was also sinus rhythm at 75/min (PR about 140 ms, QRS 80 ms) but with a very flat, late T wave giving QT about 510 ms with RR 804 ms -> QTc about 568 ms. The QTc has therefore shortened by well over 60 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR variation <2%), with upright P waves in I/II/aVF (P axis about +53) and a fixed PR of about 200 ms - at the upper limit of normal but not clearly beyond it, so first-degree AV block is not called. QRS 86 ms, QT 279 ms with RR 498 ms -> QTc 395 ms. Frontal axis +48 (normal). Compared with the previous ECG of 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR about 185 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 401 ms, axis +47) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 6 ms).

Sinus bradycardia, 54/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01). Each QRS is preceded by a P wave that begins about 218 ms before the QRS onset (biphasic, initial positive then negative in II/aVF and V1), giving a prolonged PR interval of about 218 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 76 ms, QT 389 ms with RR 1102 ms -> QTc 370 ms. Frontal QRS axis +2 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2024-11-30 (sinus 51/min, PR about 195 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 353 ms) the PR has lengthened slightly but there is no new bundle branch block, no rhythm change and no 60 ms QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 152/min. RR intervals vary 0.26-0.56 s (coefficient of variation 0.19, normalised RMSSD 0.26) with only 25% of cycles within 10% of the median, and no organised P wave is present, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 90 ms, QT 256 ms with RR 394 ms -> QTc 407 ms. Frontal QRS axis -19 (normal); no bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-09-12 (107374881) showed sinus rhythm at 77/min with a clear P wave in II/I, PR about 155 ms, QRS 90 ms and QTc 407 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 73/min, essentially regular, with upright P waves in II (0.21 mV, P axis about +55); PR about 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 355 ms with RR 818 ms -> QTc 392 ms. Frontal QRS axis +13 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block; this matches the 2025-11-23 note documenting sinus rhythm. The previous ECG of 2025-11-21 (105362569) was also sinus rhythm (67/min, PR about 165 ms, QRS 82 ms) but with QT 495 ms and RR 892 ms -> QTc 524 ms. The QTc has shortened by about 132 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min. The dominant cycle length is very stable at 0.80-0.82 s, but there are two runs of premature beats mid-recording (coupling intervals 0.17-0.51 s) accounting for the high overall RR variability; the underlying rhythm is sinus with frequent ectopy rather than atrial fibrillation, because a reproducible upright P wave (0.11 mV in II, P axis about +15) precedes each conducted sinus beat with a fixed PR of about 185 ms. QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 808 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +58 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +62); PR about 170 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 286 ms with RR 538 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +35 (normal). Very deep S waves in V1-V2 (V1 net -51 mV*ms) consistent with left ventricular hypertrophy, but no bundle branch block. No atrial flutter is present on this tracing despite the coded history. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR about 180 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 389 ms, axis +28) there is no change.

Underlying sinus rhythm at 61/min. A reproducible P wave (0.05 mV in II, 0.11 mV in I, deeply negative second component in V1) begins about 205 ms before each conducted QRS, so the PR interval is about 205 ms - borderline at the upper limit, reported without calling first-degree AV block. RR variability is increased (coefficient of variation 0.20) because of interpolated wide premature ventricular complexes, but 78% of cycles are within 10% of the median and organised P waves are present, so this is sinus rhythm with ventricular ectopy, not atrial fibrillation. QRS 90 ms, QT 371 ms with RR 976 ms -> QTc 375 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -30 (borderline normal/left). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart; the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded later the same day is not captured on this tracing.

Regular rhythm at 69/min (RR coefficient of variation 0.02) with a reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with PR about 150 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT 354 ms with RR 866 ms -> QTc 380 ms. The frontal plane is markedly abnormal: the net QRS is negative in lead I (-8.5 mV*ms), aVL and II and only slightly negative in aVF, giving a computed frontal QRS axis of about -173, i.e. an extreme (right superior) axis. The P wave and T wave are also inverted in leads I and II while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression with a tall V6 R and deep V1/V2 S waves, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation - the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with a low-amplitude upright P wave in II/I; PR about 150 ms, QRS 92 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT 489 ms with RR 858 ms -> Bazett QTc 528 ms. Frontal QRS axis +38 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2020-06-17 (sinus tachycardia 133/min, PR about 150 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 303 ms, QTc 450 ms) the QTc has increased by about 78 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold. The patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with an upright P wave in II (0.13 mV); PR about 140 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 419 ms with RR 881 ms -> QTc 446 ms (upper normal). Frontal QRS axis +68 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; this tracing was obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started and the QTc is below the 500 ms review threshold.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +56); PR about 180 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 1136 ms -> QTc 355 ms. Frontal QRS axis -7 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2018-12-13 (sinus 66/min, PR about 200 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 383 ms, axis +7) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 28 ms).

Sinus rhythm, 68/min, regular, upright P in II (0.16 mV), P axis about +76, PR 135 ms, QRS 84 ms. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad low-amplitude T wave: QT 481 ms with RR 880 ms -> Bazett QTc 513 ms. Frontal axis +48 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-11-23 (sinus 75/min, PR 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 353 ms, axis +22) the QTc has lengthened by about 160 ms, which meets the 60 ms threshold; this ECG is the most recent tracing and the patient is on escitalopram (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. The ventricular response is fast but strikingly regular at 141/min (RR 0.404-0.456 s, coefficient of variation 0.02), and there is no sinus P wave; instead the baseline shows continuous regular atrial deflections at about 280/min - two per QRS cycle, one buried in the ST-T segment (negative trough in II/aVF about 130 ms before the QRS) and one immediately pre-QRS - giving the characteristic sawtooth appearance. No true PR interval is measurable. QRS 76 ms, QT 275 ms with RR 426 ms -> QTc 422 ms. Frontal QRS axis +2 (normal); no bundle branch block, and no paced complexes are seen despite the coded cardiac pacemaker. The previous ECG of 2022-07-11 (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation - grossly irregular RR 0.38-0.82 s, coefficient of variation 0.24, no organised atrial activity - at a mean 110/min with QRS 76 ms and QTc 433 ms. Atrial fibrillation has therefore been replaced by new atrial flutter; the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 82/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with a broad upright P wave in II/I and a deep negative terminal P component in V1 suggesting left atrial enlargement; PR about 185 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 375 ms with RR 728 ms -> QTc 440 ms. Frontal QRS axis +30 (normal). PR is at the upper limit but does not exceed 200 ms, so no first-degree AV block is reported, and there is no bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with an upright P wave in II (0.13 mV) and a deep negative P component in V1 (-0.16 mV); PR about 165 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 333 ms with RR 660 ms -> QTc 410 ms. Frontal QRS axis -17 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2021-05-16 (sinus 87/min, PR about 155 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 390 ms, axis +30) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 20 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 61/min with first-degree AV block and left bundle branch block. A reproducible upright P wave in II/I/aVF begins about 220 ms before the QRS, so the PR interval is prolonged at about 220 ms. The QRS is wide at 124 ms with a broad monophasic negative complex in V1-V2 (V1 net -31 mV*ms, no terminal R') and a broad notched positive R in I, aVL and V6 without a terminal S wave - a left bundle branch block pattern. QT 448 ms with RR 984 ms -> QTc 452 ms. Frontal QRS axis -21 (normal). Compared with the previous ECG of 2024-06-03 (sinus 68/min, PR about 225 ms, QRS 126 ms, same LBBB pattern, QTc 455 ms, axis -28) there is no change: the bundle branch block and AV block were already present and the QTc is unchanged (difference 3 ms).

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with upright P waves in I and II (P axis about +41); PR about 150 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 331 ms with RR 590 ms -> QTc 431 ms. Frontal QRS axis +46 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2025-03-18 (sinus 102/min, PR about 145 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 429 ms, axis +41) the tracings are essentially identical - no change.

Sinus rhythm at 66/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with an upright P wave in II (0.11 mV, P axis about +37); PR about 155 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 365 ms with RR 911 ms -> QTc 382 ms. Frontal QRS axis -20 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 58/min, now regular (RR 0.97-1.10 s, coefficient of variation 0.04), with a reproducible low-amplitude upright P wave in II/aVF (P axis about +65) beginning about 200 ms before the QRS - PR at the upper limit of normal. QRS 82 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a very broad late T wave: QT 550 ms with RR 1042 ms -> Bazett QTc 539 ms. Frontal QRS axis +34 (normal); tall V6 R wave but no bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2022-04-06 (100867733) showed atrial fibrillation - chaotically irregular RR 0.32-0.62 s, coefficient of variation 0.19, no organised P wave - at a mean 130/min with QRS 82 ms and QTc 456 ms. Atrial fibrillation has therefore resolved to sinus rhythm, and the QTc has lengthened by about 83 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold. The patient is on amiodarone (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia at 107/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with prominent upright P waves in II (0.23 mV, P axis about +63) and a deep negative P component in V1; the P wave begins about 170 ms before the QRS. PR about 170 ms, QRS 64 ms, QT 319 ms with RR 560 ms -> QTc 426 ms. Frontal QRS axis +55 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2019-07-27 (sinus 75/min, PR about 160 ms, QRS 64 ms, QTc 420 ms, axis +45) the only difference is the faster rate; rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), P waves upright in II/aVF (P axis about +83), PR about 150 ms, QRS 76 ms. QT 297 ms with RR 498 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +68 (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular, with clear upright P waves in II/aVF (P axis about +67) beginning about 150 ms before the QRS; PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 319 ms with RR 591 ms -> QTc 415 ms. Frontal axis +57 (normal); prominent precordial voltages but no bundle branch block. Compared with the immediately preceding tracing 34 seconds earlier on the same day (sinus 100/min, PR 155 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 416 ms, axis +60) the two are essentially identical - no change.

Sinus bradycardia, 52/min, very regular (RR 1.14-1.18 s), with low-amplitude but reproducible upright P waves in II (0.07 mV) and negative terminal P in V1; PR about 170 ms, QRS 84 ms. QT 429 ms with RR 1160 ms -> QTc 398 ms. Frontal axis +36 (normal). Very large V6 R wave (3.1 mV) and deep V1 S wave suggest left ventricular hypertrophy. No AV block on this tracing despite a coded history of Mobitz II, and no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57/min with one premature beat, PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia, 121/min, regular, upright P in I/II (P axis about +38), PR about 140 ms, QRS now narrow at 86 ms. QT 298 ms with RR 494 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis +135, i.e. right axis deviation (net QRS negative in lead I, positive in aVF). No bundle branch block on this tracing. The previous ECG the same morning (106516875, 2024-12-05 01:33) showed QRS 146 ms with a broad terminal R' in V1 (net V1 positive +28.6) and wide terminal S waves in I/V6 - complete right bundle branch block, matching the RBBB coded that day - with QTc 475 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a late broad T wave: QT 513 ms with RR 968 ms -> Bazett QTc 522 ms. Frontal axis +65 (normal); no bundle branch block. arguments.explanation: Underlying sinus rhythm at 61/min. A reproducible P wave (0.05 mV in II, 0.11 mV in I, deeply negative second component in V1) begins about 205 ms before each conducted QRS, so the PR interval is about 205 ms - borderline at the upper limit, reported without calling first-degree AV block. RR variability is increased (coefficient of variation 0.20) because of interpolated wide premature ventricular complexes, but 78% of cycles are within 10% of the median and organised P waves are present, so this is sinus rhythm with ventricular ectopy, not atrial fibrillation. QRS 90 ms, QT 371 ms with RR 976 ms -> QTc 375 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -30 (borderline normal/left). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart; the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded later the same day is not captured on this tracing.

arguments.explanation: Regular rhythm at 69/min (RR coefficient of variation 0.02) with a reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with PR about 150 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT 354 ms with RR 866 ms -> QTc 380 ms. The frontal plane is markedly abnormal: the net QRS is negative in lead I (-8.5 mV*ms), aVL and II and only slightly negative in aVF, giving a computed frontal QRS axis of about -173, i.e. an extreme (right superior) axis. The P wave and T wave are also inverted in leads I and II while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression with a tall V6 R and deep V1/V2 S waves, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation - the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

arguments.explanation: Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. The ventricular response is fast but strikingly regular at 141/min (RR 0.404-0.456 s, coefficient of variation 0.02), and there is no sinus P wave; instead the baseline shows continuous regular atrial deflections at about 280/min - two per QRS cycle, one buried in the ST-T segment (negative trough in II/aVF about 130 ms before the QRS) and one immediately pre-QRS - giving the characteristic sawtooth appearance. No true PR interval is measurable. QRS 76 ms, QT 275 ms with RR 426 ms -> QTc 422 ms. Frontal QRS axis +2 (normal); no bundle branch block, and no paced complexes are seen despite the coded cardiac pacemaker. The previous ECG of 2022-07-11 (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation - grossly irregular RR 0.38-0.82 s, coefficient of variation 0.24, no organised atrial activity - at a mean 110/min with QRS 76 ms and QTc 433 ms. Atrial fibrillation has therefore been replaced by new atrial flutter; the QTc is unchanged.

Compared with the previous ECG of 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR about 185 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 401 ms, axis +47) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 6 ms).

Sinus rhythm, 68/min, regular, upright P in II (0.16 mV), P axis about +76, PR 135 ms, QRS 84 ms. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad low-amplitude T wave: QT 481 ms with RR 880 ms -> Bazett QTc 513 ms. Frontal axis +48 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-11-23 (sinus 75/min, PR 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 353 ms, axis +22) the QTc has lengthened by about 160 ms, which meets the 60 ms threshold; this ECG is the most recent tracing and the patient is on escitalopram (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), P waves upright in II/aVF (P axis about +83), PR about 150 ms, QRS 76 ms. QT 297 ms with RR 498 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +68 (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular, with clear upright P waves in II/aVF (P axis about +67) beginning about 150 ms before the QRS; PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 319 ms with RR 591 ms -> QTc 415 ms. Frontal axis +57 (normal); prominent precordial voltages but no bundle branch block. Compared with the immediately preceding tracing 34 seconds earlier on the same day (sinus 100/min, PR 155 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 416 ms, axis +60) the two are essentially identical - no change.

Sinus bradycardia, 52/min, very regular (RR 1.14-1.18 s), with low-amplitude but reproducible upright P waves in II (0.07 mV) and negative terminal P in V1; PR about 170 ms, QRS 84 ms. QT 429 ms with RR 1160 ms -> QTc 398 ms. Frontal axis +36 (normal). Very large V6 R wave (3.1 mV) and deep V1 S wave suggest left ventricular hypertrophy. No AV block on this tracing despite a coded history of Mobitz II, and no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57/min with one premature beat, PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia, 121/min, regular, upright P in I/II (P axis about +38), PR about 140 ms, QRS now narrow at 86 ms. QT 298 ms with RR 494 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis +135, i.e. right axis deviation (net QRS negative in lead I, positive in aVF). No bundle branch block on this tracing. The previous ECG the same morning (106516875, 2024-12-05 01:33) showed QRS 146 ms with a broad terminal R' in V1 (net V1 positive +28.6) and wide terminal S waves in I/V6 - complete right bundle branch block, matching the RBBB coded that day - with QTc 475 ms. The bundle branch block has resolved on the later tracing; the QTc fell 51 ms, which does not reach the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 104/min, regular, with large upright P waves in I/II (0.22 mV, P axis about +48) and a deep negative P component in V1; PR about 150 ms, QRS 92 ms. Sinus tachycardia, 109/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.03), with upright P waves in I and II; PR about 145 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 346 ms with RR 548 ms -> QTc 467 ms (mildly prolonged; Bazett over-corrects at this rate). Frontal QRS axis +36 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 144/min. RR intervals range 0.30-0.60 s (coefficient of variation 0.16, normalised RMSSD 0.22) with only 57% of cycles within 10% of the median, and there is no organised P wave - the deflection preceding the QRS is negative in I and II and not reproducible, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 90 ms, QT 291 ms with RR 416 ms -> QTc 452 ms. Frontal axis +3 (normal); no bundle branch block. The previous ECG, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same evening (107914094), also showed atrial fibrillation at 140/min with QRS 90 ms and QTc 444 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of the same morning recorded 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 0.864-0.882 s) with a small, reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS that is positive in lead I (+0.07 mV) but negative in II and aVF (-0.04 and -0.07 mV) and biphasic in V1, giving a P axis of about -45. This inverted inferior P axis with a fixed PR indicates a low atrial/ectopic atrial (non-sinus) rhythm rather than sinus rhythm, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER. PR 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 396 ms with RR 873 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis -24 (normal). No bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-04-27 also showed a regular 60/min rhythm with negative P waves in II (QTc 397 ms) but with a globally inverted lead I suggesting arm-lead reversal; there is no change in rhythm category, bundle branch block or QTc (difference 27 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.02), with upright P waves in II/aVF (0.18 mV, P axis about +76); PR about 125 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT 306 ms with RR 616 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +6 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with a small upright P wave in II and a biphasic P in V1; PR about 140 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 373 ms with RR 832 ms -> QTc 409 ms. Frontal QRS axis +20 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; note this remains the most recent tracing despite escitalopram having been started on 2026-08-01.

Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR variation <2%), with upright P waves in I/II/aVF (P axis about +53) and a fixed PR of about 200 ms - at the upper limit of normal but not clearly beyond it, so first-degree AV block is not called. QRS 86 ms, QT 279 ms with RR 498 ms -> QTc 395 ms. Frontal axis +48 (normal). Compared with the previous ECG of 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR about 185 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 401 ms, axis +47) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 6 ms).

Sinus rhythm, 68/min, regular, upright P in II (0.16 mV), P axis about +76, PR 135 ms, QRS 84 ms. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad low-amplitude T wave: QT 481 ms with RR 880 ms -> Bazett QTc 513 ms. Frontal axis +48 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-11-23 (sinus 75/min, PR 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 353 ms, axis +22) the QTc has lengthened by about 160 ms, which meets the 60 ms threshold; this ECG is the most recent tracing and the patient is on escitalopram (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), P waves upright in II/aVF (P axis about +83), PR about 150 ms, QRS 76 ms. QT 297 ms with RR 498 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +68 (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular, with clear upright P waves in II/aVF (P axis about +67) beginning about 150 ms before the QRS; PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 319 ms with RR 591 ms -> QTc 415 ms. Frontal axis +57 (normal); prominent precordial voltages but no bundle branch block. Compared with the immediately preceding tracing 34 seconds earlier on the same day (sinus 100/min, PR 155 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 416 ms, axis +60) the two are essentially identical - no change.

Sinus bradycardia, 52/min, very regular (RR 1.14-1.18 s), with low-amplitude but reproducible upright P waves in II (0.07 mV) and negative terminal P in V1; PR about 170 ms, QRS 84 ms. QT 429 ms with RR 1160 ms -> QTc 398 ms. Frontal axis +36 (normal). Very large V6 R wave (3.1 mV) and deep V1 S wave suggest left ventricular hypertrophy. No AV block on this tracing despite a coded history of Mobitz II, and no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57/min with one premature beat, PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia, 121/min, regular, upright P in I/II (P axis about +38), PR about 140 ms, QRS now narrow at 86 ms. QT 298 ms with RR 494 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis +135, i.e. right axis deviation (net QRS negative in lead I, positive in aVF). No bundle branch block on this tracing. The previous ECG the same morning (106516875, 2024-12-05 01:33) showed QRS 146 ms with a broad terminal R' in V1 (net V1 positive +28.6) and wide terminal S waves in I/V6 - complete right bundle branch block, matching the RBBB coded that day - with QTc 475 ms. The bundle branch block has resolved on the later tracing; the QTc fell 51 ms, which does not reach the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus rhythm, 62/min, regular (RR variation 1%), with a small but consistent P wave (0.06 mV spatial, negative component in V1) starting about 170 ms before the QRS; PR about 170 ms, QRS 90 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a late broad T wave: QT 513 ms with RR 968 ms -> Bazett QTc 522 ms. Frontal axis +65 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2025-06-07 (sinus bradycardia 47/min, PR about 185 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 409 ms) the QTc has increased by about 113 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold - consistent with amiodarone started 2025-11-10 (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean 101/min. RR intervals vary from 0.40 to 0.98 s (coefficient of variation 0.28, normalised RMSSD 0.41) and only 38% of cycles lie within 10% of the median. No organised P wave can be identified in any lead - the pre-QRS segment shows only fibrillatory activity of 20-50 microvolts - so no PR interval is measurable. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; the patient carries a coded diagnosis of atrial fibrillation from the same admission and is on warfarin.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 144/min. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 0.864-0.882 s) with a small, reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS that is positive in lead I (+0.07 mV) but negative in II and aVF (-0.04 and -0.07 mV) and biphasic in V1, giving a P axis of about -45. This inverted inferior P axis with a fixed PR indicates a low atrial/ectopic atrial (non-sinus) rhythm rather than sinus rhythm, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER. PR 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 396 ms with RR 873 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis -24 (normal). No bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-04-27 also showed a regular 60/min rhythm with negative P waves in II (QTc 397 ms) but with a globally inverted lead I suggesting arm-lead reversal; there is no change in rhythm category, bundle branch block or QTc (difference 27 ms).

No previous ECG in the chart, so no comparison possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 104/min, regular, with large upright P waves in I/II (0.22 mV, P axis about +48) and a deep negative P component in V1; PR about 150 ms, QRS 92 ms. QT 358 ms with RR 579 ms -> QTc 470 ms. Frontal axis +39 (normal); no bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-06-20 also showed sinus rhythm but at 147/min, where the T wave merges with the following P wave so the QT cannot be measured reliably (estimates range from about 275 to 360 ms, QTc 430-565 ms); no confident QTc change of 60 ms or more can be asserted, and rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia, 109/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.03), with upright P waves in I and II; PR about 145 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 346 ms with RR 548 ms -> QTc 467 ms (mildly prolonged; Bazett over-corrects at this rate). Frontal QRS axis +36 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 144/min. RR intervals range 0.30-0.60 s (coefficient of variation 0.16, normalised RMSSD 0.22) with only 57% of cycles within 10% of the median, and there is no organised P wave - the deflection preceding the QRS is negative in I and II and not reproducible, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 90 ms, QT 291 ms with RR 416 ms -> QTc 452 ms. Frontal axis +3 (normal); no bundle branch block. The previous ECG, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same evening (107914094), also showed atrial fibrillation at 140/min with QRS 90 ms and QTc 444 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of the same morning recorded 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 0.864-0.882 s) with a small, reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS that is positive in lead I (+0.07 mV) but negative in II and aVF (-0.04 and -0.07 mV) and biphasic in V1, giving a P axis of about -45. This inverted inferior P axis with a fixed PR indicates a low atrial/ectopic atrial (non-sinus) rhythm rather than sinus rhythm, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER. PR 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 396 ms with RR 873 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis -24 (normal). No bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-04-27 also showed a regular 60/min rhythm with negative P waves in II (QTc 397 ms) but with a globally inverted lead I suggesting arm-lead reversal; there is no change in rhythm category, bundle branch block or QTc (difference 27 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.02), with upright P waves in II/aVF (0.18 mV, P axis about +76); PR about 125 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT 306 ms with RR 616 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR variation <2%), with upright P waves in I/II/aVF (P axis about +53) and a fixed PR of about 200 ms - at the upper limit of normal but not clearly beyond it, so first-degree AV block is not called. Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), P waves upright in II/aVF (P axis about +83), PR about 150 ms, QRS 76 ms. QT 297 ms with RR 498 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +68 (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Compared with the previous ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57/min with one premature beat, PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia, 121/min, regular, upright P in I/II (P axis about +38), PR about 140 ms, QRS now narrow at 86 ms. QT 298 ms with RR 494 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Sinus rhythm, 62/min, regular (RR variation 1%), with a small but consistent P wave (0.06 mV spatial, negative component in V1) starting about 170 ms before the QRS; PR about 170 ms, QRS 90 ms. Atrial fibrillation with rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean 101/min. RR intervals vary from 0.40 to 0.98 s (coefficient of variation 0.28, normalised RMSSD 0.41) and only 38% of cycles lie within 10% of the median. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; the patient carries a coded diagnosis of atrial fibrillation from the same admission and is on warfarin.

Sinus tachycardia, 109/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.03), with upright P waves in I and II; PR about 145 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 346 ms with RR 548 ms -> QTc 467 ms (mildly prolonged; Bazett over-corrects at this rate). Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 144/min. The previous ECG, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same evening (107914094), also showed atrial fibrillation at 140/min with QRS 90 ms and QTc 444 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of the same morning recorded 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 0.864-0.882 s) with a small, reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS that is positive in lead I (+0.07 mV) but negative in II and aVF (-0.04 and -0.07 mV) and biphasic in V1, giving a P axis of about -45. This inverted inferior P axis with a fixed PR indicates a low atrial/ectopic atrial (non-sinus) rhythm rather than sinus rhythm, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER. PR 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 396 ms with RR 873 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis -24 (normal). No bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-04-27 also showed a regular 60/min rhythm with negative P waves in II (QTc 397 ms) but with a globally inverted lead I suggesting arm-lead reversal; there is no change in rhythm category, bundle branch block or QTc (difference 27 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.02), with upright P waves in II/aVF (0.18 mV, P axis about +76); PR about 125 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT 306 ms with RR 616 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +6 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean 53/min. Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), with upright P waves in I/II/aVF; PR about 155 ms, QRS 64 ms, QT 337 ms with RR 720 ms -> QTc 397 ms. Frontal QRS axis +52 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

The QTc has therefore shortened by well over 60 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR variation <2%), with upright P waves in I/II/aVF (P axis about +53) and a fixed PR of about 200 ms - at the upper limit of normal but not clearly beyond it, so first-degree AV block is not called. Compared with the previous ECG of 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR about 185 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 401 ms, axis +47) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 6 ms).

Sinus rhythm, 68/min, regular, upright P in II (0.16 mV), P axis about +76, PR 135 ms, QRS 84 ms. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad low-amplitude T wave: QT 481 ms with RR 880 ms -> Bazett QTc 513 ms. Frontal axis +48 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-11-23 (sinus 75/min, PR 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 353 ms, axis +22) the QTc has lengthened by about 160 ms, which meets the 60 ms threshold; this ECG is the most recent tracing and the patient is on escitalopram (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), P waves upright in II/aVF (P axis about +83), PR about 150 ms, QRS 76 ms. QT 297 ms with RR 498 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +68 (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular, with clear upright P waves in II/aVF (P axis about +67) beginning about 150 ms before the QRS; PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 319 ms with RR 591 ms -> QTc 415 ms. Frontal axis +57 (normal); prominent precordial voltages but no bundle branch block. Compared with the immediately preceding tracing 34 seconds earlier on the same day (sinus 100/min, PR 155 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 416 ms, axis +60) the two are essentially identical - no change.

Sinus bradycardia, 52/min, very regular (RR 1.14-1.18 s), with low-amplitude but reproducible upright P waves in II (0.07 mV) and negative terminal P in V1; PR about 170 ms, QRS 84 ms. QT 429 ms with RR 1160 ms -> QTc 398 ms. Frontal axis +36 (normal). Very large V6 R wave (3.1 mV) and deep V1 S wave suggest left ventricular hypertrophy. No AV block on this tracing despite a coded history of Mobitz II, and no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57/min with one premature beat, PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia, 121/min, regular, upright P in I/II (P axis about +38), PR about 140 ms, QRS now narrow at 86 ms. QT 298 ms with RR 494 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis +135, i.e. right axis deviation (net QRS negative in lead I, positive in aVF). No bundle branch block on this tracing. The previous ECG the same morning (106516875, 2024-12-05 01:33) showed QRS 146 ms with a broad terminal R' in V1 (net V1 positive +28.6) and wide terminal S waves in I/V6 - complete right bundle branch block, matching the RBBB coded that day - with QTc 475 ms. The bundle branch block has resolved on the later tracing; the QTc fell 51 ms, which does not reach the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus rhythm, 62/min, regular (RR variation 1%), with a small but consistent P wave (0.06 mV spatial, negative component in V1) starting about 170 ms before the QRS; PR about 170 ms, QRS 90 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a late broad T wave: QT 513 ms with RR 968 ms -> Bazett QTc 522 ms. Frontal axis +65 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2025-06-07 (sinus bradycardia 47/min, PR about 185 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 409 ms) the QTc has increased by about 113 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold - consistent with amiodarone started 2025-11-10 (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean 101/min. RR intervals vary from 0.40 to 0.98 s (coefficient of variation 0.28, normalised RMSSD 0.41) and only 38% of cycles lie within 10% of the median. No organised P wave can be identified in any lead - the pre-QRS segment shows only fibrillatory activity of 20-50 microvolts - so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 74 ms, QT 309 ms with RR 595 ms -> QTc 400 ms. Frontal QRS axis -61, left axis deviation. No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; the patient carries a coded diagnosis of atrial fibrillation from the same admission and is on warfarin.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 0.864-0.882 s) with a small, reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS that is positive in lead I (+0.07 mV) but negative in II and aVF (-0.04 and -0.07 mV) and biphasic in V1, giving a P axis of about -45. This inverted inferior P axis with a fixed PR indicates a low atrial/ectopic atrial (non-sinus) rhythm rather than sinus rhythm, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER. PR 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 396 ms with RR 873 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis -24 (normal). No bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-04-27 also showed a regular 60/min rhythm with negative P waves in II (QTc 397 ms) but with a globally inverted lead I suggesting arm-lead reversal; there is no change in rhythm category, bundle branch block or QTc (difference 27 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.02), with upright P waves in II/aVF (0.18 mV, P axis about +76); PR about 125 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT 306 ms with RR 616 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 104/min, regular, with large upright P waves in I/II (0.22 mV, P axis about +48) and a deep negative P component in V1; PR about 150 ms, QRS 92 ms. QT 358 ms with RR 579 ms -> QTc 470 ms. Frontal axis +39 (normal); no bundle branch block. Sinus tachycardia, 109/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.03), with upright P waves in I and II; PR about 145 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 346 ms with RR 548 ms -> QTc 467 ms (mildly prolonged; Bazett over-corrects at this rate). Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 144/min. RR intervals range 0.30-0.60 s (coefficient of variation 0.16, normalised RMSSD 0.22) with only 57% of cycles within 10% of the median, and there is no organised P wave - the deflection preceding the QRS is negative in I and II and not reproducible, so no PR interval is measurable. The previous ECG, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same evening (107914094), also showed atrial fibrillation at 140/min with QRS 90 ms and QTc 444 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of the same morning recorded 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 0.864-0.882 s) with a small, reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS that is positive in lead I (+0.07 mV) but negative in II and aVF (-0.04 and -0.07 mV) and biphasic in V1, giving a P axis of about -45. This inverted inferior P axis with a fixed PR indicates a low atrial/ectopic atrial (non-sinus) rhythm rather than sinus rhythm, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER. PR 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 396 ms with RR 873 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis -24 (normal). No bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-04-27 also showed a regular 60/min rhythm with negative P waves in II (QTc 397 ms) but with a globally inverted lead I suggesting arm-lead reversal; there is no change in rhythm category, bundle branch block or QTc (difference 27 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.02), with upright P waves in II/aVF (0.18 mV, P axis about +76); PR about 125 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT 306 ms with RR 616 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +6 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with a small upright P wave in II and a biphasic P in V1; PR about 140 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 373 ms with RR 832 ms -> QTc 409 ms. Frontal QRS axis +20 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean 53/min. Compared with the previous ECG of 2025-03-08 (sinus 62/min, PR about 116 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 437 ms, axis +61) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 23 ms). Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), with upright P waves in I/II/aVF; PR about 155 ms, QRS 64 ms, QT 337 ms with RR 720 ms -> QTc 397 ms. Frontal QRS axis +52 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR variation <2%), with upright P waves in I/II/aVF (P axis about +53) and a fixed PR of about 200 ms - at the upper limit of normal but not clearly beyond it, so first-degree AV block is not called. Sinus bradycardia, 54/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01). Each QRS is preceded by a P wave that begins about 218 ms before the QRS onset (biphasic, initial positive then negative in II/aVF and V1), giving a prolonged PR interval of about 218 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 76 ms, QT 389 ms with RR 1102 ms -> QTc 370 ms. Frontal QRS axis +2 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2024-11-30 (sinus 51/min, PR about 195 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 353 ms) the PR has lengthened slightly but there is no new bundle branch block, no rhythm change and no 60 ms QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 152/min. RR intervals vary 0.26-0.56 s (coefficient of variation 0.19, normalised RMSSD 0.26) with only 25% of cycles within 10% of the median, and no organised P wave is present, so no PR interval is measurable. The previous ECG of 2025-09-12 (107374881) showed sinus rhythm at 77/min with a clear P wave in II/I, PR about 155 ms, QRS 90 ms and QTc 407 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 73/min, essentially regular, with upright P waves in II (0.21 mV, P axis about +55); PR about 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 355 ms with RR 818 ms -> QTc 392 ms. Frontal QRS axis +13 (normal). The QTc has shortened by about 132 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min. The dominant cycle length is very stable at 0.80-0.82 s, but there are two runs of premature beats mid-recording (coupling intervals 0.17-0.51 s) accounting for the high overall RR variability; the underlying rhythm is sinus with frequent ectopy rather than atrial fibrillation, because a reproducible upright P wave (0.11 mV in II, P axis about +15) precedes each conducted sinus beat with a fixed PR of about 185 ms. QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 808 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +58 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +62); PR about 170 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 286 ms with RR 538 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +35 (normal). Very deep S waves in V1-V2 (V1 net -51 mV*ms) consistent with left ventricular hypertrophy, but no bundle branch block. No atrial flutter is present on this tracing despite the coded history. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR about 180 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 389 ms, axis +28) there is no change.

Underlying sinus rhythm at 61/min. A reproducible P wave (0.05 mV in II, 0.11 mV in I, deeply negative second component in V1) begins about 205 ms before each conducted QRS, so the PR interval is about 205 ms - borderline at the upper limit, reported without calling first-degree AV block. RR variability is increased (coefficient of variation 0.20) because of interpolated wide premature ventricular complexes, but 78% of cycles are within 10% of the median and organised P waves are present, so this is sinus rhythm with ventricular ectopy, not atrial fibrillation. QRS 90 ms, QT 371 ms with RR 976 ms -> QTc 375 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -30 (borderline normal/left). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart; the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded later the same day is not captured on this tracing.

Sinus rhythm, 68/min, regular, upright P in II (0.16 mV), P axis about +76, PR 135 ms, QRS 84 ms. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-11-23 (sinus 75/min, PR 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 353 ms, axis +22) the QTc has lengthened by about 160 ms, which meets the 60 ms threshold; this ECG is the most recent tracing and the patient is on escitalopram (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular, with clear upright P waves in II/aVF (P axis about +67) beginning about 150 ms before the QRS; PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 319 ms with RR 591 ms -> QTc 415 ms. arguments.explanation: Regular rhythm at 69/min (RR coefficient of variation 0.02) with a reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with PR about 150 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT 354 ms with RR 866 ms -> QTc 380 ms. The frontal plane is markedly abnormal: the net QRS is negative in lead I (-8.5 mV*ms), aVL and II and only slightly negative in aVF, giving a computed frontal QRS axis of about -173, i.e. an extreme (right superior) axis. The P wave and T wave are also inverted in leads I and II while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression with a tall V6 R and deep V1/V2 S waves, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation - the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia, 109/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.03), with upright P waves in I and II; PR about 145 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 346 ms with RR 548 ms -> QTc 467 ms (mildly prolonged; Bazett over-corrects at this rate). Frontal QRS axis +36 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 144/min. RR intervals range 0.30-0.60 s (coefficient of variation 0.16, normalised RMSSD 0.22) with only 57% of cycles within 10% of the median, and there is no organised P wave - the deflection preceding the QRS is negative in I and II and not reproducible, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 90 ms, QT 291 ms with RR 416 ms -> QTc 452 ms. Frontal axis +3 (normal); no bundle branch block. The previous ECG, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same evening (107914094), also showed atrial fibrillation at 140/min with QRS 90 ms and QTc 444 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of the same morning recorded 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 0.864-0.882 s) with a small, reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS that is positive in lead I (+0.07 mV) but negative in II and aVF (-0.04 and -0.07 mV) and biphasic in V1, giving a P axis of about -45. This inverted inferior P axis with a fixed PR indicates a low atrial/ectopic atrial (non-sinus) rhythm rather than sinus rhythm, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER. PR 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 396 ms with RR 873 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis -24 (normal). No bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-04-27 also showed a regular 60/min rhythm with negative P waves in II (QTc 397 ms) but with a globally inverted lead I suggesting arm-lead reversal; there is no change in rhythm category, bundle branch block or QTc (difference 27 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.02), with upright P waves in II/aVF (0.18 mV, P axis about +76); PR about 125 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT 306 ms with RR 616 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +6 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with a small upright P wave in II and a biphasic P in V1; PR about 140 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 373 ms with RR 832 ms -> QTc 409 ms. Frontal QRS axis +20 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; note this remains the most recent tracing despite escitalopram having been started on 2026-08-01.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean 53/min. RR intervals range 0.78-1.60 s (coefficient of variation 0.20, normalised RMSSD 0.29) with only 56% of cycles within 10% of the median, and the TP/PR segments are flat in lead II with no identifiable P wave, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 88 ms, QT 425 ms with RR 1128 ms -> QTc 400 ms. Frontal QRS axis +3 (normal); deep V1/V2 S waves but no bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2024-11-12 (107873952) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with a clear 0.22 mV P wave in II, PR 190 ms, QRS 78 ms and QTc 396 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new on this tracing; the QTc is unchanged (difference 4 ms).

Sinus bradycardia, 58/min, regular, with upright P waves in II (0.16 mV, P axis about +75); PR about 120 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 421 ms with RR 1030 ms -> QTc 414 ms. Frontal QRS axis +62 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2025-03-08 (sinus 62/min, PR about 116 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 437 ms, axis +61) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 23 ms). This remains the most recent tracing although haloperidol was started on 2026-09-15.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), with upright P waves in I/II/aVF; PR about 155 ms, QRS 64 ms, QT 337 ms with RR 720 ms -> QTc 397 ms. Frontal QRS axis +52 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 77/min, regular, with prominent upright P waves in II (0.27 mV, P axis about +76); PR about 160 ms, QRS 62 ms, QT 402 ms with RR 783 ms -> QTc 454 ms. Frontal QRS axis +63 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2020-02-02 (109048192) was also sinus rhythm at 75/min (PR about 140 ms, QRS 80 ms) but with a very flat, late T wave giving QT about 510 ms with RR 804 ms -> QTc about 568 ms. The QTc has therefore shortened by well over 60 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR variation <2%), with upright P waves in I/II/aVF (P axis about +53) and a fixed PR of about 200 ms - at the upper limit of normal but not clearly beyond it, so first-degree AV block is not called. QRS 86 ms, QT 279 ms with RR 498 ms -> QTc 395 ms. Frontal axis +48 (normal). Compared with the previous ECG of 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR about 185 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 401 ms, axis +47) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 6 ms).

Sinus bradycardia, 54/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01). Each QRS is preceded by a P wave that begins about 218 ms before the QRS onset (biphasic, initial positive then negative in II/aVF and V1), giving a prolonged PR interval of about 218 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 76 ms, QT 389 ms with RR 1102 ms -> QTc 370 ms. Frontal QRS axis +2 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2024-11-30 (sinus 51/min, PR about 195 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 353 ms) the PR has lengthened slightly but there is no new bundle branch block, no rhythm change and no 60 ms QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 152/min. RR intervals vary 0.26-0.56 s (coefficient of variation 0.19, normalised RMSSD 0.26) with only 25% of cycles within 10% of the median, and no organised P wave is present, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 90 ms, QT 256 ms with RR 394 ms -> QTc 407 ms. Frontal QRS axis -19 (normal); no bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-09-12 (107374881) showed sinus rhythm at 77/min with a clear P wave in II/I, PR about 155 ms, QRS 90 ms and QTc 407 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 73/min, essentially regular, with upright P waves in II (0.21 mV, P axis about +55); PR about 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 355 ms with RR 818 ms -> QTc 392 ms. Frontal QRS axis +13 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block; this matches the 2025-11-23 note documenting sinus rhythm. The previous ECG of 2025-11-21 (105362569) was also sinus rhythm (67/min, PR about 165 ms, QRS 82 ms) but with QT 495 ms and RR 892 ms -> QTc 524 ms. The QTc has shortened by about 132 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min. The dominant cycle length is very stable at 0.80-0.82 s, but there are two runs of premature beats mid-recording (coupling intervals 0.17-0.51 s) accounting for the high overall RR variability; the underlying rhythm is sinus with frequent ectopy rather than atrial fibrillation, because a reproducible upright P wave (0.11 mV in II, P axis about +15) precedes each conducted sinus beat with a fixed PR of about 185 ms. QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 808 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +58 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +62); PR about 170 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 286 ms with RR 538 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +35 (normal). Very deep S waves in V1-V2 (V1 net -51 mV*ms) consistent with left ventricular hypertrophy, but no bundle branch block. No atrial flutter is present on this tracing despite the coded history. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR about 180 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 389 ms, axis +28) there is no change.

Underlying sinus rhythm at 61/min. A reproducible P wave (0.05 mV in II, 0.11 mV in I, deeply negative second component in V1) begins about 205 ms before each conducted QRS, so the PR interval is about 205 ms - borderline at the upper limit, reported without calling first-degree AV block. RR variability is increased (coefficient of variation 0.20) because of interpolated wide premature ventricular complexes, but 78% of cycles are within 10% of the median and organised P waves are present, so this is sinus rhythm with ventricular ectopy, not atrial fibrillation. QRS 90 ms, QT 371 ms with RR 976 ms -> QTc 375 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -30 (borderline normal/left). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart; the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded later the same day is not captured on this tracing.

Regular rhythm at 69/min (RR coefficient of variation 0.02) with a reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with PR about 150 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT 354 ms with RR 866 ms -> QTc 380 ms. The frontal plane is markedly abnormal: the net QRS is negative in lead I (-8.5 mV*ms), aVL and II and only slightly negative in aVF, giving a computed frontal QRS axis of about -173, i.e. an extreme (right superior) axis. The P wave and T wave are also inverted in leads I and II while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression with a tall V6 R and deep V1/V2 S waves, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation - the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm, 68/min, regular, upright P in II (0.16 mV), P axis about +76, PR 135 ms, QRS 84 ms. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad low-amplitude T wave: QT 481 ms with RR 880 ms -> Bazett QTc 513 ms. Frontal axis +48 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-11-23 (sinus 75/min, PR 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 353 ms, axis +22) the QTc has lengthened by about 160 ms, which meets the 60 ms threshold; this ECG is the most recent tracing and the patient is on escitalopram (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), P waves upright in II/aVF (P axis about +83), PR about 150 ms, QRS 76 ms. QT 297 ms with RR 498 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +68 (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular, with clear upright P waves in II/aVF (P axis about +67) beginning about 150 ms before the QRS; PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 319 ms with RR 591 ms -> QTc 415 ms. Frontal axis +57 (normal); prominent precordial voltages but no bundle branch block. Compared with the immediately preceding tracing 34 seconds earlier on the same day (sinus 100/min, PR 155 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 416 ms, axis +60) the two are essentially identical - no change.

Sinus bradycardia, 52/min, very regular (RR 1.14-1.18 s), with low-amplitude but reproducible upright P waves in II (0.07 mV) and negative terminal P in V1; PR about 170 ms, QRS 84 ms. QT 429 ms with RR 1160 ms -> QTc 398 ms. Frontal axis +36 (normal). Very large V6 R wave (3.1 mV) and deep V1 S wave suggest left ventricular hypertrophy. No AV block on this tracing despite a coded history of Mobitz II, and no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57/min with one premature beat, PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia, 121/min, regular, upright P in I/II (P axis about +38), PR about 140 ms, QRS now narrow at 86 ms. QT 298 ms with RR 494 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis +135, i.e. right axis deviation (net QRS negative in lead I, positive in aVF). No bundle branch block on this tracing. The previous ECG the same morning (106516875, 2024-12-05 01:33) showed QRS 146 ms with a broad terminal R' in V1 (net V1 positive +28.6) and wide terminal S waves in I/V6 - complete right bundle branch block, matching the RBBB coded that day - with QTc 475 ms. The bundle branch block has resolved on the later tracing; the QTc fell 51 ms, which does not reach the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus rhythm, 62/min, regular (RR variation 1%), with a small but consistent P wave (0.06 mV spatial, negative component in V1) starting about 170 ms before the QRS; PR about 170 ms, QRS 90 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a late broad T wave: QT 513 ms with RR 968 ms -> Bazett QTc 522 ms. Frontal axis +65 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2025-06-07 (sinus bradycardia 47/min, PR about 185 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 409 ms) the QTc has increased by about 113 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold - consistent with amiodarone started 2025-11-10 (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean 101/min. RR intervals vary from 0.40 to 0.98 s (coefficient of variation 0.28, normalised RMSSD 0.41) and only 38% of cycles lie within 10% of the median. No organised P wave can be identified in any lead - the pre-QRS segment shows only fibrillatory activity of 20-50 microvolts - so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 74 ms, QT 309 ms with RR 595 ms -> QTc 400 ms. Frontal QRS axis -61, left axis deviation. No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; the patient carries a coded diagnosis of atrial fibrillation from the same admission and is on warfarin.

arguments.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with a low-amplitude upright P wave in II/I; PR about 150 ms, QRS 92 ms. Guideline-recommended anticoagulation is absent - needs prescriber review.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) has been prescribed since 2022-03-01; the current order c6f532e9 (2026-08-22, valid to 2027-01-05) is active at 2026-09-24, together with warfarin and metoprolol succinate. This 95-year-old patient on amiodarone plus a beta blocker with a QTc of 539 ms requires prescriber review per the QT monitoring memo of 2025-01-15; no ECG has been repeated since 2022.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (first-ever citalopram order c17946a1). Because the start date is on or after 2026-03-01 the revised memo of 2026-03-01 applies: ECG required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, and shows sinus rhythm at 81/min with QTc 378 ms. Requirement satisfied within the window.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (order e578297f; the drug first appears on the medication list in the 2025-11-10 note). The start date falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-02-28, so the 2025-09-01 memo applies: ECG within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start. Requirement satisfied within the window - although that ECG showed QTc 522 ms, which is raised separately as a QT safety item.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (first-ever escitalopram order 88943096). Start date on or after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo of 2026-03-01 applies: ECG required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (order 4dde586a; the drug is absent from the 2026-06-24 note and present in the 2026-08-01 note). No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722), so as of 2026-09-24 the requirement is unmet and overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (order f757652a). That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09 (104253928, QTc 414 ms), but at the evaluation time of 2026-09-24 12:00 the deadline has not yet passed, so the requirement is not yet due.

Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' - a warfarin dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician after 2026-03-01, so the 2026-03-01 memo requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation d6b3bad5), four days after the change. Requirement satisfied within the window.

Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol' - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist acting under the anticoagulation standing order, after 2026-03-01. The 2026-03-01 memo therefore requires a clinic INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR(PT) in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change; no INR has been resulted since. As of 2026-09-24 the follow-up INR is overdue.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation (Condition 42731, encounter 2025-08-22) carried in the cardiology clinic problem list in all notes from 2025-10-10 to 2026-07-28.
