Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 0.864-0.882 s) with a small, reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS that is positive in lead I (+0.07 mV) but negative in II and aVF (-0.04 and -0.07 mV) and biphasic in V1, giving a P axis of about -45. This inverted inferior P axis with a fixed PR indicates a low atrial/ectopic atrial (non-sinus) rhythm rather than sinus rhythm, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER. PR 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 396 ms with RR 873 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis -24 (normal). No bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-04-27 also showed a regular 60/min rhythm with negative P waves in II (QTc 397 ms) but with a globally inverted lead I suggesting arm-lead reversal; there is no change in rhythm category, bundle branch block or QTc (difference 27 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 74/min. QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 808 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +58 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +62); PR about 170 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 286 ms with RR 538 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +35 (normal). Very deep S waves in V1-V2 (V1 net -51 mV*ms) consistent with left ventricular hypertrophy, but no bundle branch block. No atrial flutter is present on this tracing despite the coded history. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR about 180 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 389 ms, axis +28) there is no change.

Underlying sinus rhythm at 61/min. A reproducible P wave (0.05 mV in II, 0.11 mV in I, deeply negative second component in V1) begins about 205 ms before each conducted QRS, so the PR interval is about 205 ms - borderline at the upper limit, reported without calling first-degree AV block. RR variability is increased (coefficient of variation 0.20) because of interpolated wide premature ventricular complexes, but 78% of cycles are within 10% of the median and organised P waves are present, so this is sinus rhythm with ventricular ectopy, not atrial fibrillation. QRS 90 ms, QT 371 ms with RR 976 ms -> QTc 375 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -30 (borderline normal/left). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart; the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded later the same day is not captured on this tracing.

Regular rhythm at 69/min (RR coefficient of variation 0.02) with a reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with PR about 150 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT 354 ms with RR 866 ms -> QTc 380 ms. The frontal plane is markedly abnormal: the net QRS is negative in lead I (-8.5 mV*ms), aVL and II and only slightly negative in aVF, giving a computed frontal QRS axis of about -173, i.e. an extreme (right superior) axis. The P wave and T wave are also inverted in leads I and II while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression with a tall V6 R and deep V1/V2 S waves, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation - the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. The ventricular response is fast but strikingly regular at 141/min (RR 0.404-0.456 s, coefficient of variation 0.02), and there is no sinus P wave; instead the baseline shows continuous regular atrial deflections at about 280/min - two per QRS cycle, one buried in the ST-T segment (negative trough in II/aVF about 130 ms before the QRS) and one immediately pre-QRS - giving the characteristic sawtooth appearance. No true PR interval is measurable. QRS 76 ms, QT 275 ms with RR 426 ms -> QTc 422 ms. Frontal QRS axis +2 (normal); no bundle branch block, and no paced complexes are seen despite the coded cardiac pacemaker. The previous ECG of 2022-07-11 (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation - grossly irregular RR 0.38-0.82 s, coefficient of variation 0.24, no organised atrial activity - at a mean 110/min with QRS 76 ms and QTc 433 ms. QRS 90 ms, QT 371 ms with RR 976 ms -> QTc 375 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -30 (borderline normal/left). No bundle branch block. Regular rhythm at 69/min (RR coefficient of variation 0.02) with a reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with PR about 150 ms. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 0.864-0.882 s) with a small, reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS that is positive in lead I (+0.07 mV) but negative in II and aVF (-0.04 and -0.07 mV) and biphasic in V1, giving a P axis of about -45. This inverted inferior P axis with a fixed PR indicates a low atrial/ectopic atrial (non-sinus) rhythm rather than sinus rhythm, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER. PR 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 396 ms with RR 873 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis -24 (normal). No bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-04-27 also showed a regular 60/min rhythm with negative P waves in II (QTc 397 ms) but with a globally inverted lead I suggesting arm-lead reversal; there is no change in rhythm category, bundle branch block or QTc (difference 27 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 73/min, essentially regular, with upright P waves in II (0.21 mV, P axis about +55); PR about 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 355 ms with RR 818 ms -> QTc 392 ms. Frontal QRS axis +13 (normal). The QTc has shortened by about 132 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min. The dominant cycle length is very stable at 0.80-0.82 s, but there are two runs of premature beats mid-recording (coupling intervals 0.17-0.51 s) accounting for the high overall RR variability; the underlying rhythm is sinus with frequent ectopy rather than atrial fibrillation, because a reproducible upright P wave (0.11 mV in II, P axis about +15) precedes each conducted sinus beat with a fixed PR of about 185 ms. QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 808 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +58 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +62); PR about 170 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 286 ms with RR 538 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +35 (normal). Very deep S waves in V1-V2 (V1 net -51 mV*ms) consistent with left ventricular hypertrophy, but no bundle branch block. No atrial flutter is present on this tracing despite the coded history. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR about 180 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 389 ms, axis +28) there is no change.

Underlying sinus rhythm at 61/min. A reproducible P wave (0.05 mV in II, 0.11 mV in I, deeply negative second component in V1) begins about 205 ms before each conducted QRS, so the PR interval is about 205 ms - borderline at the upper limit, reported without calling first-degree AV block. RR variability is increased (coefficient of variation 0.20) because of interpolated wide premature ventricular complexes, but 78% of cycles are within 10% of the median and organised P waves are present, so this is sinus rhythm with ventricular ectopy, not atrial fibrillation. QRS 90 ms, QT 371 ms with RR 976 ms -> QTc 375 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -30 (borderline normal/left). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart; the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded later the same day is not captured on this tracing.

Regular rhythm at 69/min (RR coefficient of variation 0.02) with a reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with PR about 150 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT 354 ms with RR 866 ms -> QTc 380 ms. The frontal plane is markedly abnormal: the net QRS is negative in lead I (-8.5 mV*ms), aVL and II and only slightly negative in aVF, giving a computed frontal QRS axis of about -173, i.e. an extreme (right superior) axis. The P wave and T wave are also inverted in leads I and II while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression with a tall V6 R and deep V1/V2 S waves, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation - the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with a low-amplitude upright P wave in II/I; PR about 150 ms, QRS 92 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT 489 ms with RR 858 ms -> Bazett QTc 528 ms. Frontal QRS axis +38 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2020-06-17 (sinus tachycardia 133/min, PR about 150 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 303 ms, QTc 450 ms) the QTc has increased by about 78 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold. The patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Frontal QRS axis +68 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; this tracing was obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started and the QTc is below the 500 ms review threshold.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +56); PR about 180 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 1136 ms -> QTc 355 ms. Frontal QRS axis -7 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2018-12-13 (sinus 66/min, PR about 200 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 383 ms, axis +7) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 28 ms).

Sinus rhythm, 68/min, regular, upright P in II (0.16 mV), P axis about +76, PR 135 ms, QRS 84 ms. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad low-amplitude T wave: QT 481 ms with RR 880 ms -> Bazett QTc 513 ms. Frontal axis +48 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-11-23 (sinus 75/min, PR 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 353 ms, axis +22) the QTc has lengthened by about 160 ms, which meets the 60 ms threshold; this ECG is the most recent tracing and the patient is on escitalopram (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. The ventricular response is fast but strikingly regular at 141/min (RR 0.404-0.456 s, coefficient of variation 0.02), and there is no sinus P wave; instead the baseline shows continuous regular atrial deflections at about 280/min - two per QRS cycle, one buried in the ST-T segment (negative trough in II/aVF about 130 ms before the QRS) and one immediately pre-QRS - giving the characteristic sawtooth appearance. No true PR interval is measurable. QRS 76 ms, QT 275 ms with RR 426 ms -> QTc 422 ms. QRS 76 ms, QT 389 ms with RR 1102 ms -> QTc 370 ms. Frontal QRS axis +2 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2024-11-30 (sinus 51/min, PR about 195 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 353 ms) the PR has lengthened slightly but there is no new bundle branch block, no rhythm change and no 60 ms QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 152/min. RR intervals vary 0.26-0.56 s (coefficient of variation 0.19, normalised RMSSD 0.26) with only 25% of cycles within 10% of the median, and no organised P wave is present, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 90 ms, QT 256 ms with RR 394 ms -> QTc 407 ms. Frontal QRS axis -19 (normal); no bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-09-12 (107374881) showed sinus rhythm at 77/min with a clear P wave in II/I, PR about 155 ms, QRS 90 ms and QTc 407 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 73/min, essentially regular, with upright P waves in II (0.21 mV, P axis about +55); PR about 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 355 ms with RR 818 ms -> QTc 392 ms. Frontal QRS axis +13 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block; this matches the 2025-11-23 note documenting sinus rhythm. The previous ECG of 2025-11-21 (105362569) was also sinus rhythm (67/min, PR about 165 ms, QRS 82 ms) but with QT 495 ms and RR 892 ms -> QTc 524 ms. The QTc has shortened by about 132 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min. The dominant cycle length is very stable at 0.80-0.82 s, but there are two runs of premature beats mid-recording (coupling intervals 0.17-0.51 s) accounting for the high overall RR variability; the underlying rhythm is sinus with frequent ectopy rather than atrial fibrillation, because a reproducible upright P wave (0.11 mV in II, P axis about +15) precedes each conducted sinus beat with a fixed PR of about 185 ms. QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 808 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +58 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +62); PR about 170 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 286 ms with RR 538 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +35 (normal). Very deep S waves in V1-V2 (V1 net -51 mV*ms) consistent with left ventricular hypertrophy, but no bundle branch block. No atrial flutter is present on this tracing despite the coded history. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR about 180 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 389 ms, axis +28) there is no change.

Underlying sinus rhythm at 61/min. A reproducible P wave (0.05 mV in II, 0.11 mV in I, deeply negative second component in V1) begins about 205 ms before each conducted QRS, so the PR interval is about 205 ms - borderline at the upper limit, reported without calling first-degree AV block. RR variability is increased (coefficient of variation 0.20) because of interpolated wide premature ventricular complexes, but 78% of cycles are within 10% of the median and organised P waves are present, so this is sinus rhythm with ventricular ectopy, not atrial fibrillation. QRS 90 ms, QT 371 ms with RR 976 ms -> QTc 375 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -30 (borderline normal/left). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart; the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded later the same day is not captured on this tracing.

Regular rhythm at 69/min (RR coefficient of variation 0.02) with a reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with PR about 150 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT 354 ms with RR 866 ms -> QTc 380 ms. The frontal plane is markedly abnormal: the net QRS is negative in lead I (-8.5 mV*ms), aVL and II and only slightly negative in aVF, giving a computed frontal QRS axis of about -173, i.e. an extreme (right superior) axis. The P wave and T wave are also inverted in leads I and II while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression with a tall V6 R and deep V1/V2 S waves, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation - the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with a low-amplitude upright P wave in II/I; PR about 150 ms, QRS 92 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT 489 ms with RR 858 ms -> Bazett QTc 528 ms. Frontal QRS axis +38 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2020-06-17 (sinus tachycardia 133/min, PR about 150 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 303 ms, QTc 450 ms) the QTc has increased by about 78 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold. The patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with an upright P wave in II (0.13 mV); PR about 140 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 419 ms with RR 881 ms -> QTc 446 ms (upper normal). Frontal QRS axis +68 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; this tracing was obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started and the QTc is below the 500 ms review threshold.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +56); PR about 180 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 1136 ms -> QTc 355 ms. Frontal QRS axis -7 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2018-12-13 (sinus 66/min, PR about 200 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 383 ms, axis +7) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 28 ms).

Sinus rhythm, 68/min, regular, upright P in II (0.16 mV), P axis about +76, PR 135 ms, QRS 84 ms. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad low-amplitude T wave: QT 481 ms with RR 880 ms -> Bazett QTc 513 ms. Frontal axis +48 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-11-23 (sinus 75/min, PR 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 353 ms, axis +22) the QTc has lengthened by about 160 ms, which meets the 60 ms threshold; this ECG is the most recent tracing and the patient is on escitalopram (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. The ventricular response is fast but strikingly regular at 141/min (RR 0.404-0.456 s, coefficient of variation 0.02), and there is no sinus P wave; instead the baseline shows continuous regular atrial deflections at about 280/min - two per QRS cycle, one buried in the ST-T segment (negative trough in II/aVF about 130 ms before the QRS) and one immediately pre-QRS - giving the characteristic sawtooth appearance. No true PR interval is measurable. QRS 76 ms, QT 275 ms with RR 426 ms -> QTc 422 ms. Frontal QRS axis +2 (normal); no bundle branch block, and no paced complexes are seen despite the coded cardiac pacemaker. The previous ECG of 2022-07-11 (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation - grossly irregular RR 0.38-0.82 s, coefficient of variation 0.24, no organised atrial activity - at a mean 110/min with QRS 76 ms and QTc 433 ms. Atrial fibrillation has therefore been replaced by new atrial flutter; the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 82/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with a broad upright P wave in II/I and a deep negative terminal P component in V1 suggesting left atrial enlargement; PR about 185 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 375 ms with RR 728 ms -> QTc 440 ms. Frontal QRS axis +30 (normal). PR is at the upper limit but does not exceed 200 ms, so no first-degree AV block is reported, and there is no bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with an upright P wave in II (0.13 mV) and a deep negative P component in V1 (-0.16 mV); PR about 165 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 333 ms with RR 660 ms -> QTc 410 ms. Frontal QRS axis -17 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2021-05-16 (sinus 87/min, PR about 155 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 390 ms, axis +30) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 20 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 61/min with first-degree AV block and left bundle branch block. A reproducible upright P wave in II/I/aVF begins about 220 ms before the QRS, so the PR interval is prolonged at about 220 ms. The QRS is wide at 124 ms with a broad monophasic negative complex in V1-V2 (V1 net -31 mV*ms, no terminal R') and a broad notched positive R in I, aVL and V6 without a terminal S wave - a left bundle branch block pattern. QT 448 ms with RR 984 ms -> QTc 452 ms. Frontal QRS axis -21 (normal). Compared with the previous ECG of 2024-06-03 (sinus 68/min, PR about 225 ms, QRS 126 ms, same LBBB pattern, QTc 455 ms, axis -28) there is no change: the bundle branch block and AV block were already present and the QTc is unchanged (difference 3 ms).

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with upright P waves in I and II (P axis about +41); PR about 150 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 331 ms with RR 590 ms -> QTc 431 ms. Frontal QRS axis +46 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2025-03-18 (sinus 102/min, PR about 145 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 429 ms, axis +41) the tracings are essentially identical - no change.

Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), P waves upright in II/aVF (P axis about +83), PR about 150 ms, QRS 76 ms. QT 297 ms with RR 498 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +68 (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular, with clear upright P waves in II/aVF (P axis about +67) beginning about 150 ms before the QRS; PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 319 ms with RR 591 ms -> QTc 415 ms. Frontal axis +57 (normal); prominent precordial voltages but no bundle branch block. Compared with the immediately preceding tracing 34 seconds earlier on the same day (sinus 100/min, PR 155 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 416 ms, axis +60) the two are essentially identical - no change.

Sinus bradycardia, 52/min, very regular (RR 1.14-1.18 s), with low-amplitude but reproducible upright P waves in II (0.07 mV) and negative terminal P in V1; PR about 170 ms, QRS 84 ms. QT 429 ms with RR 1160 ms -> QTc 398 ms. Frontal axis +36 (normal). Very large V6 R wave (3.1 mV) and deep V1 S wave suggest left ventricular hypertrophy. No AV block on this tracing despite a coded history of Mobitz II, and no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57/min with one premature beat, PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia, 121/min, regular, upright P in I/II (P axis about +38), PR about 140 ms, QRS now narrow at 86 ms. QT 298 ms with RR 494 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis +135, i.e. right axis deviation (net QRS negative in lead I, positive in aVF). No bundle branch block on this tracing. The previous ECG the same morning (106516875, 2024-12-05 01:33) showed QRS 146 ms with a broad terminal R' in V1 (net V1 positive +28.6) and wide terminal S waves in I/V6 - complete right bundle branch block, matching the RBBB coded that day - with QTc 475 ms. The bundle branch block has resolved on the later tracing; the QTc fell 51 ms, which does not reach the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus rhythm, 62/min, regular (RR variation 1%), with a small but consistent P wave (0.06 mV spatial, negative component in V1) starting about 170 ms before the QRS; PR about 170 ms, QRS 90 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a late broad T wave: QT 513 ms with RR 968 ms -> Bazett QTc 522 ms. Frontal axis +65 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2025-06-07 (sinus bradycardia 47/min, PR about 185 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 409 ms) the QTc has increased by about 113 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold - consistent with amiodarone started 2025-11-10 (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean 101/min. RR intervals vary from 0.40 to 0.98 s (coefficient of variation 0.28, normalised RMSSD 0.41) and only 38% of cycles lie within 10% of the median. No organised P wave can be identified in any lead - the pre-QRS segment shows only fibrillatory activity of 20-50 microvolts - so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 74 ms, QT 309 ms with RR 595 ms -> QTc 400 ms. Frontal QRS axis -61, left axis deviation. No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; the patient carries a coded diagnosis of atrial fibrillation from the same admission and is on warfarin.

Needs prescriber review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic visit (order dc397aff, valid 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28, active at 2026-09-24) despite the outside-records summary of 2026-08-12, which documents an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and states that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Anticoagulant continuation after a major GI bleed needs prescriber review.

Both orders remain in force at 2026-09-24 and neither has been stopped, so the patient (paroxysmal AF/flutter, CLL) is exposed to duplicate full-dose anticoagulation. Needs immediate clarification of which agent is intended.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no organised P waves (RR 0.30-0.60 s, RR coefficient of variation 0.16-0.19) at a mean rate of 140-144/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - not sinus rhythm at 72. Unspecified atrial fibrillation (Condition 54ec94da-144c-5ec2-a135-76f7a52d00ac) was also coded at the 2026-06-10 18:36 encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the chart needs correction and the rate/rhythm reassessed.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm, 81/min (RR 0.66-0.86 s, gradual respiratory variation), upright consistent P in II/aVF (0.22 mV) and biphasic in V1, P axis about +74. PR 190 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 326 ms with RR 744 ms -> Bazett QTc 378 ms. Frontal QRS axis +48 (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. No previous ECG in the chart, so no comparison possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 104/min, regular, with large upright P waves in I/II (0.22 mV, P axis about +48) and a deep negative P component in V1; PR about 150 ms, QRS 92 ms. QT 358 ms with RR 579 ms -> QTc 470 ms. Frontal axis +39 (normal); no bundle branch block. Sinus tachycardia, 109/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.03), with upright P waves in I and II; PR about 145 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 346 ms with RR 548 ms -> QTc 467 ms (mildly prolonged; Bazett over-corrects at this rate). Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 144/min. RR intervals range 0.30-0.60 s (coefficient of variation 0.16, normalised RMSSD 0.22) with only 57% of cycles within 10% of the median, and there is no organised P wave - the deflection preceding the QRS is negative in I and II and not reproducible, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 90 ms, QT 291 ms with RR 416 ms -> QTc 452 ms. Frontal axis +3 (normal); no bundle branch block. The previous ECG, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same evening (107914094), also showed atrial fibrillation at 140/min with QRS 90 ms and QTc 444 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of the same morning recorded 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 0.864-0.882 s) with a small, reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS that is positive in lead I (+0.07 mV) but negative in II and aVF (-0.04 and -0.07 mV) and biphasic in V1, giving a P axis of about -45. This inverted inferior P axis with a fixed PR indicates a low atrial/ectopic atrial (non-sinus) rhythm rather than sinus rhythm, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER. PR 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 396 ms with RR 873 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis -24 (normal). No bundle branch block. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 152/min. RR intervals vary 0.26-0.56 s (coefficient of variation 0.19, normalised RMSSD 0.26) with only 25% of cycles within 10% of the median, and no organised P wave is present, so no PR interval is measurable. Sinus rhythm at 73/min, essentially regular, with upright P waves in II (0.21 mV, P axis about +55); PR about 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 355 ms with RR 818 ms -> QTc 392 ms. Frontal QRS axis +13 (normal). The QTc has shortened by about 132 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min. The dominant cycle length is very stable at 0.80-0.82 s, but there are two runs of premature beats mid-recording (coupling intervals 0.17-0.51 s) accounting for the high overall RR variability; the underlying rhythm is sinus with frequent ectopy rather than atrial fibrillation, because a reproducible upright P wave (0.11 mV in II, P axis about +15) precedes each conducted sinus beat with a fixed PR of about 185 ms. QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 808 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +58 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +62); PR about 170 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 286 ms with RR 538 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +35 (normal). Very deep S waves in V1-V2 (V1 net -51 mV*ms) consistent with left ventricular hypertrophy, but no bundle branch block. No atrial flutter is present on this tracing despite the coded history. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR about 180 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 389 ms, axis +28) there is no change.

Underlying sinus rhythm at 61/min. A reproducible P wave (0.05 mV in II, 0.11 mV in I, deeply negative second component in V1) begins about 205 ms before each conducted QRS, so the PR interval is about 205 ms - borderline at the upper limit, reported without calling first-degree AV block. RR variability is increased (coefficient of variation 0.20) because of interpolated wide premature ventricular complexes, but 78% of cycles are within 10% of the median and organised P waves are present, so this is sinus rhythm with ventricular ectopy, not atrial fibrillation. QRS 90 ms, QT 371 ms with RR 976 ms -> QTc 375 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -30 (borderline normal/left). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart; the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded later the same day is not captured on this tracing.

Regular rhythm at 69/min (RR coefficient of variation 0.02) with a reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with PR about 150 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT 354 ms with RR 866 ms -> QTc 380 ms. The frontal plane is markedly abnormal: the net QRS is negative in lead I (-8.5 mV*ms), aVL and II and only slightly negative in aVF, giving a computed frontal QRS axis of about -173, i.e. an extreme (right superior) axis. The P wave and T wave are also inverted in leads I and II while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression with a tall V6 R and deep V1/V2 S waves, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation - the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with a low-amplitude upright P wave in II/I; PR about 150 ms, QRS 92 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT 489 ms with RR 858 ms -> Bazett QTc 528 ms. Frontal QRS axis +38 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2020-06-17 (sinus tachycardia 133/min, PR about 150 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 303 ms, QTc 450 ms) the QTc has increased by about 78 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold. The patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with an upright P wave in II (0.13 mV); PR about 140 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 419 ms with RR 881 ms -> QTc 446 ms (upper normal). Frontal QRS axis +68 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +56); PR about 180 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 1136 ms -> QTc 355 ms. Frontal QRS axis -7 (normal). Compared with the previous ECG of 2018-12-13 (sinus 66/min, PR about 200 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 383 ms, axis +7) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 28 ms).

Sinus rhythm, 68/min, regular, upright P in II (0.16 mV), P axis about +76, PR 135 ms, QRS 84 ms. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad low-amplitude T wave: QT 481 ms with RR 880 ms -> Bazett QTc 513 ms. Frontal axis +48 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-11-23 (sinus 75/min, PR 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 353 ms, axis +22) the QTc has lengthened by about 160 ms, which meets the 60 ms threshold; this ECG is the most recent tracing and the patient is on escitalopram (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. The ventricular response is fast but strikingly regular at 141/min (RR 0.404-0.456 s, coefficient of variation 0.02), and there is no sinus P wave; instead the baseline shows continuous regular atrial deflections at about 280/min - two per QRS cycle, one buried in the ST-T segment (negative trough in II/aVF about 130 ms before the QRS) and one immediately pre-QRS - giving the characteristic sawtooth appearance. No true PR interval is measurable. QRS 76 ms, QT 275 ms with RR 426 ms -> QTc 422 ms. Frontal QRS axis +2 (normal); no bundle branch block, and no paced complexes are seen despite the coded cardiac pacemaker. The previous ECG of 2022-07-11 (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation - grossly irregular RR 0.38-0.82 s, coefficient of variation 0.24, no organised atrial activity - at a mean 110/min with QRS 76 ms and QTc 433 ms. Atrial fibrillation has therefore been replaced by new atrial flutter; the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 82/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with a broad upright P wave in II/I and a deep negative terminal P component in V1 suggesting left atrial enlargement; PR about 185 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 375 ms with RR 728 ms -> QTc 440 ms. Frontal QRS axis +30 (normal). PR is at the upper limit but does not exceed 200 ms, so no first-degree AV block is reported, and there is no bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with an upright P wave in II (0.13 mV) and a deep negative P component in V1 (-0.16 mV); PR about 165 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 333 ms with RR 660 ms -> QTc 410 ms. Sinus rhythm at 61/min with first-degree AV block and left bundle branch block. A reproducible upright P wave in II/I/aVF begins about 220 ms before the QRS, so the PR interval is prolonged at about 220 ms. The QRS is wide at 124 ms with a broad monophasic negative complex in V1-V2 (V1 net -31 mV*ms, no terminal R') and a broad notched positive R in I, aVL and V6 without a terminal S wave - a left bundle branch block pattern. QT 448 ms with RR 984 ms -> QTc 452 ms. Frontal QRS axis -21 (normal). Sinus bradycardia, 52/min, very regular (RR 1.14-1.18 s), with low-amplitude but reproducible upright P waves in II (0.07 mV) and negative terminal P in V1; PR about 170 ms, QRS 84 ms. QT 429 ms with RR 1160 ms -> QTc 398 ms. Frontal axis +36 (normal). Very large V6 R wave (3.1 mV) and deep V1 S wave suggest left ventricular hypertrophy. Sinus tachycardia, 121/min, regular, upright P in I/II (P axis about +38), PR about 140 ms, QRS now narrow at 86 ms. QT 298 ms with RR 494 ms -> QTc 424 ms. arguments.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 58/min, now regular (RR 0.97-1.10 s, coefficient of variation 0.04), with a reproducible low-amplitude upright P wave in II/aVF (P axis about +65) beginning about 200 ms before the QRS - PR at the upper limit of normal. Needs immediate clarification of which agent is intended.

The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the chart needs correction and the rate/rhythm reassessed.

The most recent ECG in the chart, 108018814 of 2023-10-08, is sinus rhythm at 68/min with a markedly prolonged repolarisation: QRS 84 ms, QT 481 ms, RR 880 ms, giving Bazett QTc 513 ms (>=500 ms). Most recent electrolytes (2025-08-23) are normal: potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, so QTc prolongation is not explained by electrolyte depletion. interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm, 81/min (RR 0.66-0.86 s, gradual respiratory variation), upright consistent P in II/aVF (0.22 mV) and biphasic in V1, P axis about +74. PR 190 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 326 ms with RR 744 ms -> Bazett QTc 378 ms. Frontal QRS axis +48 (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Despite a history of atrial fibrillation and citalopram/apixaban therapy, this tracing is in sinus rhythm, consistent with the 2026-03-07 note. No previous ECG in the chart, so no comparison possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 104/min, regular, with large upright P waves in I/II (0.22 mV, P axis about +48) and a deep negative P component in V1; PR about 150 ms, QRS 92 ms. QT 358 ms with RR 579 ms -> QTc 470 ms. Frontal axis +39 (normal); no bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-06-20 also showed sinus rhythm but at 147/min, where the T wave merges with the following P wave so the QT cannot be measured reliably (estimates range from about 275 to 360 ms, QTc 430-565 ms); no confident QTc change of 60 ms or more can be asserted, and rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia, 109/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.03), with upright P waves in I and II; PR about 145 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 346 ms with RR 548 ms -> QTc 467 ms (mildly prolonged; Bazett over-corrects at this rate). Frontal QRS axis +36 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 144/min. RR intervals range 0.30-0.60 s (coefficient of variation 0.16, normalised RMSSD 0.22) with only 57% of cycles within 10% of the median, and there is no organised P wave - the deflection preceding the QRS is negative in I and II and not reproducible, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 90 ms, QT 291 ms with RR 416 ms -> QTc 452 ms. Frontal axis +3 (normal); no bundle branch block. The previous ECG, recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same evening (107914094), also showed atrial fibrillation at 140/min with QRS 90 ms and QTc 444 ms, so there is no change. Note that the clinic note of the same morning recorded 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 0.864-0.882 s) with a small, reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS that is positive in lead I (+0.07 mV) but negative in II and aVF (-0.04 and -0.07 mV) and biphasic in V1, giving a P axis of about -45. This inverted inferior P axis with a fixed PR indicates a low atrial/ectopic atrial (non-sinus) rhythm rather than sinus rhythm, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER. PR 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 396 ms with RR 873 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis -24 (normal). No bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-04-27 also showed a regular 60/min rhythm with negative P waves in II (QTc 397 ms) but with a globally inverted lead I suggesting arm-lead reversal; there is no change in rhythm category, bundle branch block or QTc (difference 27 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.02), with upright P waves in II/aVF (0.18 mV, P axis about +76); PR about 125 ms, QRS 68 ms, QT 306 ms with RR 616 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +6 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with a small upright P wave in II and a biphasic P in V1; PR about 140 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 373 ms with RR 832 ms -> QTc 409 ms. Frontal QRS axis +20 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; note this remains the most recent tracing despite escitalopram having been started on 2026-08-01.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean 53/min. RR intervals range 0.78-1.60 s (coefficient of variation 0.20, normalised RMSSD 0.29) with only 56% of cycles within 10% of the median, and the TP/PR segments are flat in lead II with no identifiable P wave, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 88 ms, QT 425 ms with RR 1128 ms -> QTc 400 ms. Frontal QRS axis +3 (normal); deep V1/V2 S waves but no bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2024-11-12 (107873952) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with a clear 0.22 mV P wave in II, PR 190 ms, QRS 78 ms and QTc 396 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new on this tracing; the QTc is unchanged (difference 4 ms).

Sinus bradycardia, 58/min, regular, with upright P waves in II (0.16 mV, P axis about +75); PR about 120 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 421 ms with RR 1030 ms -> QTc 414 ms. Frontal QRS axis +62 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2025-03-08 (sinus 62/min, PR about 116 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 437 ms, axis +61) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 23 ms). This remains the most recent tracing although haloperidol was started on 2026-09-15.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), with upright P waves in I/II/aVF; PR about 155 ms, QRS 64 ms, QT 337 ms with RR 720 ms -> QTc 397 ms. Frontal QRS axis +52 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 77/min, regular, with prominent upright P waves in II (0.27 mV, P axis about +76); PR about 160 ms, QRS 62 ms, QT 402 ms with RR 783 ms -> QTc 454 ms. Frontal QRS axis +63 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2020-02-02 (109048192) was also sinus rhythm at 75/min (PR about 140 ms, QRS 80 ms) but with a very flat, late T wave giving QT about 510 ms with RR 804 ms -> QTc about 568 ms. The QTc has therefore shortened by well over 60 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR variation <2%), with upright P waves in I/II/aVF (P axis about +53) and a fixed PR of about 200 ms - at the upper limit of normal but not clearly beyond it, so first-degree AV block is not called. QRS 86 ms, QT 279 ms with RR 498 ms -> QTc 395 ms. Frontal axis +48 (normal). Compared with the previous ECG of 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR about 185 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 401 ms, axis +47) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 6 ms).

Sinus bradycardia, 54/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01). Each QRS is preceded by a P wave that begins about 218 ms before the QRS onset (biphasic, initial positive then negative in II/aVF and V1), giving a prolonged PR interval of about 218 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 76 ms, QT 389 ms with RR 1102 ms -> QTc 370 ms. Frontal QRS axis +2 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2024-11-30 (sinus 51/min, PR about 195 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 353 ms) the PR has lengthened slightly but there is no new bundle branch block, no rhythm change and no 60 ms QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 152/min. RR intervals vary 0.26-0.56 s (coefficient of variation 0.19, normalised RMSSD 0.26) with only 25% of cycles within 10% of the median, and no organised P wave is present, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 90 ms, QT 256 ms with RR 394 ms -> QTc 407 ms. Frontal QRS axis -19 (normal); no bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-09-12 (107374881) showed sinus rhythm at 77/min with a clear P wave in II/I, PR about 155 ms, QRS 90 ms and QTc 407 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 73/min, essentially regular, with upright P waves in II (0.21 mV, P axis about +55); PR about 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 355 ms with RR 818 ms -> QTc 392 ms. Frontal QRS axis +13 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block; this matches the 2025-11-23 note documenting sinus rhythm. The previous ECG of 2025-11-21 (105362569) was also sinus rhythm (67/min, PR about 165 ms, QRS 82 ms) but with QT 495 ms and RR 892 ms -> QTc 524 ms. The QTc has shortened by about 132 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min. The dominant cycle length is very stable at 0.80-0.82 s, but there are two runs of premature beats mid-recording (coupling intervals 0.17-0.51 s) accounting for the high overall RR variability; the underlying rhythm is sinus with frequent ectopy rather than atrial fibrillation, because a reproducible upright P wave (0.11 mV in II, P axis about +15) precedes each conducted sinus beat with a fixed PR of about 185 ms. QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 808 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +58 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +62); PR about 170 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 286 ms with RR 538 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +35 (normal). Very deep S waves in V1-V2 (V1 net -51 mV*ms) consistent with left ventricular hypertrophy, but no bundle branch block. No atrial flutter is present on this tracing despite the coded history. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR about 180 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 389 ms, axis +28) there is no change.

Underlying sinus rhythm at 61/min. A reproducible P wave (0.05 mV in II, 0.11 mV in I, deeply negative second component in V1) begins about 205 ms before each conducted QRS, so the PR interval is about 205 ms - borderline at the upper limit, reported without calling first-degree AV block. RR variability is increased (coefficient of variation 0.20) because of interpolated wide premature ventricular complexes, but 78% of cycles are within 10% of the median and organised P waves are present, so this is sinus rhythm with ventricular ectopy, not atrial fibrillation. QRS 90 ms, QT 371 ms with RR 976 ms -> QTc 375 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -30 (borderline normal/left). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart; the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded later the same day is not captured on this tracing.

Regular rhythm at 69/min (RR coefficient of variation 0.02) with a reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with PR about 150 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT 354 ms with RR 866 ms -> QTc 380 ms. The frontal plane is markedly abnormal: the net QRS is negative in lead I (-8.5 mV*ms), aVL and II and only slightly negative in aVF, giving a computed frontal QRS axis of about -173, i.e. an extreme (right superior) axis. The P wave and T wave are also inverted in leads I and II while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression with a tall V6 R and deep V1/V2 S waves, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation - the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with a low-amplitude upright P wave in II/I; PR about 150 ms, QRS 92 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT 489 ms with RR 858 ms -> Bazett QTc 528 ms. Frontal QRS axis +38 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2020-06-17 (sinus tachycardia 133/min, PR about 150 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 303 ms, QTc 450 ms) the QTc has increased by about 78 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold. The patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with an upright P wave in II (0.13 mV); PR about 140 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 419 ms with RR 881 ms -> QTc 446 ms (upper normal). Frontal QRS axis +68 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; this tracing was obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started and the QTc is below the 500 ms review threshold.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +56); PR about 180 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 1136 ms -> QTc 355 ms. Frontal QRS axis -7 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2018-12-13 (sinus 66/min, PR about 200 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 383 ms, axis +7) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 28 ms).

Sinus rhythm, 68/min, regular, upright P in II (0.16 mV), P axis about +76, PR 135 ms, QRS 84 ms. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad low-amplitude T wave: QT 481 ms with RR 880 ms -> Bazett QTc 513 ms. Frontal axis +48 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-11-23 (sinus 75/min, PR 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 353 ms, axis +22) the QTc has lengthened by about 160 ms, which meets the 60 ms threshold; this ECG is the most recent tracing and the patient is on escitalopram (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. The ventricular response is fast but strikingly regular at 141/min (RR 0.404-0.456 s, coefficient of variation 0.02), and there is no sinus P wave; instead the baseline shows continuous regular atrial deflections at about 280/min - two per QRS cycle, one buried in the ST-T segment (negative trough in II/aVF about 130 ms before the QRS) and one immediately pre-QRS - giving the characteristic sawtooth appearance. No true PR interval is measurable. QRS 76 ms, QT 275 ms with RR 426 ms -> QTc 422 ms. Frontal QRS axis +2 (normal); no bundle branch block, and no paced complexes are seen despite the coded cardiac pacemaker. The previous ECG of 2022-07-11 (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation - grossly irregular RR 0.38-0.82 s, coefficient of variation 0.24, no organised atrial activity - at a mean 110/min with QRS 76 ms and QTc 433 ms. Atrial fibrillation has therefore been replaced by new atrial flutter; the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 82/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with a broad upright P wave in II/I and a deep negative terminal P component in V1 suggesting left atrial enlargement; PR about 185 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 375 ms with RR 728 ms -> QTc 440 ms. Frontal QRS axis +30 (normal). PR is at the upper limit but does not exceed 200 ms, so no first-degree AV block is reported, and there is no bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with an upright P wave in II (0.13 mV) and a deep negative P component in V1 (-0.16 mV); PR about 165 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 333 ms with RR 660 ms -> QTc 410 ms. Frontal QRS axis -17 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2021-05-16 (sinus 87/min, PR about 155 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 390 ms, axis +30) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (difference 20 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 61/min with first-degree AV block and left bundle branch block. A reproducible upright P wave in II/I/aVF begins about 220 ms before the QRS, so the PR interval is prolonged at about 220 ms. The QRS is wide at 124 ms with a broad monophasic negative complex in V1-V2 (V1 net -31 mV*ms, no terminal R') and a broad notched positive R in I, aVL and V6 without a terminal S wave - a left bundle branch block pattern. QT 448 ms with RR 984 ms -> QTc 452 ms. Frontal QRS axis -21 (normal). Compared with the previous ECG of 2024-06-03 (sinus 68/min, PR about 225 ms, QRS 126 ms, same LBBB pattern, QTc 455 ms, axis -28) there is no change: the bundle branch block and AV block were already present and the QTc is unchanged (difference 3 ms).

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with upright P waves in I and II (P axis about +41); PR about 150 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 331 ms with RR 590 ms -> QTc 431 ms. Frontal QRS axis +46 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2025-03-18 (sinus 102/min, PR about 145 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 429 ms, axis +41) the tracings are essentially identical - no change.

Sinus rhythm at 66/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with an upright P wave in II (0.11 mV, P axis about +37); PR about 155 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 365 ms with RR 911 ms -> QTc 382 ms. Frontal QRS axis -20 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), P waves upright in II/aVF (P axis about +83), PR about 150 ms, QRS 76 ms. QT 297 ms with RR 498 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +68 (normal). No conduction abnormality. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular, with clear upright P waves in II/aVF (P axis about +67) beginning about 150 ms before the QRS; PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 319 ms with RR 591 ms -> QTc 415 ms. Frontal axis +57 (normal); prominent precordial voltages but no bundle branch block. Compared with the immediately preceding tracing 34 seconds earlier on the same day (sinus 100/min, PR 155 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 416 ms, axis +60) the two are essentially identical - no change.

Sinus bradycardia, 52/min, very regular (RR 1.14-1.18 s), with low-amplitude but reproducible upright P waves in II (0.07 mV) and negative terminal P in V1; PR about 170 ms, QRS 84 ms. QT 429 ms with RR 1160 ms -> QTc 398 ms. Frontal axis +36 (normal). Very large V6 R wave (3.1 mV) and deep V1 S wave suggest left ventricular hypertrophy. No AV block on this tracing despite a coded history of Mobitz II, and no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57/min with one premature beat, PR about 155 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia, 121/min, regular, upright P in I/II (P axis about +38), PR about 140 ms, QRS now narrow at 86 ms. QT 298 ms with RR 494 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis +135, i.e. right axis deviation (net QRS negative in lead I, positive in aVF). No bundle branch block on this tracing. The previous ECG the same morning (106516875, 2024-12-05 01:33) showed QRS 146 ms with a broad terminal R' in V1 (net V1 positive +28.6) and wide terminal S waves in I/V6 - complete right bundle branch block, matching the RBBB coded that day - with QTc 475 ms. The bundle branch block has resolved on the later tracing; the QTc fell 51 ms, which does not reach the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus rhythm, 62/min, regular (RR variation 1%), with a small but consistent P wave (0.06 mV spatial, negative component in V1) starting about 170 ms before the QRS; PR about 170 ms, QRS 90 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a late broad T wave: QT 513 ms with RR 968 ms -> Bazett QTc 522 ms. Frontal axis +65 (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the previous ECG of 2025-06-07 (sinus bradycardia 47/min, PR about 185 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 409 ms) the QTc has increased by about 113 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold - consistent with amiodarone started 2025-11-10 (raised separately as a QT safety item).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean 101/min. RR intervals vary from 0.40 to 0.98 s (coefficient of variation 0.28, normalised RMSSD 0.41) and only 38% of cycles lie within 10% of the median. No organised P wave can be identified in any lead - the pre-QRS segment shows only fibrillatory activity of 20-50 microvolts - so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 74 ms, QT 309 ms with RR 595 ms -> QTc 400 ms. Frontal QRS axis -61, left axis deviation. No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; the patient carries a coded diagnosis of atrial fibrillation from the same admission and is on warfarin.

The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the chart needs correction and the rate/rhythm reassessed.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 0.864-0.882 s) with a small, reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS that is positive in lead I (+0.07 mV) but negative in II and aVF (-0.04 and -0.07 mV) and biphasic in V1, giving a P axis of about -45. This inverted inferior P axis with a fixed PR indicates a low atrial/ectopic atrial (non-sinus) rhythm rather than sinus rhythm, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER. PR 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 396 ms with RR 873 ms -> QTc 424 ms. Frontal QRS axis -24 (normal). No bundle branch block. The previous ECG of 2025-04-27 also showed a regular 60/min rhythm with negative P waves in II (QTc 397 ms) but with a globally inverted lead I suggesting arm-lead reversal; there is no change in rhythm category, bundle branch block or QTc (difference 27 ms).

Sinus tachycardia, 120/min, regular (RR variation <2%), with upright P waves in I/II/aVF (P axis about +53) and a fixed PR of about 200 ms - at the upper limit of normal but not clearly beyond it, so first-degree AV block is not called. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 152/min. Sinus rhythm at 73/min, essentially regular, with upright P waves in II (0.21 mV, P axis about +55); PR about 175 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 355 ms with RR 818 ms -> QTc 392 ms. Frontal QRS axis +13 (normal). The QTc has shortened by about 132 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min. The dominant cycle length is very stable at 0.80-0.82 s, but there are two runs of premature beats mid-recording (coupling intervals 0.17-0.51 s) accounting for the high overall RR variability; the underlying rhythm is sinus with frequent ectopy rather than atrial fibrillation, because a reproducible upright P wave (0.11 mV in II, P axis about +15) precedes each conducted sinus beat with a fixed PR of about 185 ms. QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 808 ms -> QTc 421 ms. Frontal QRS axis +58 (normal). No AV or bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation <1%), with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +62); PR about 170 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 286 ms with RR 538 ms -> QTc 390 ms. Frontal QRS axis +35 (normal). Very deep S waves in V1-V2 (V1 net -51 mV*ms) consistent with left ventricular hypertrophy, but no bundle branch block. No atrial flutter is present on this tracing despite the coded history. Compared with the previous ECG of 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR about 180 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 389 ms, axis +28) there is no change.

Underlying sinus rhythm at 61/min. A reproducible P wave (0.05 mV in II, 0.11 mV in I, deeply negative second component in V1) begins about 205 ms before each conducted QRS, so the PR interval is about 205 ms - borderline at the upper limit, reported without calling first-degree AV block. RR variability is increased (coefficient of variation 0.20) because of interpolated wide premature ventricular complexes, but 78% of cycles are within 10% of the median and organised P waves are present, so this is sinus rhythm with ventricular ectopy, not atrial fibrillation. QRS 90 ms, QT 371 ms with RR 976 ms -> QTc 375 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -30 (borderline normal/left). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart; the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded later the same day is not captured on this tracing.

Regular rhythm at 69/min (RR coefficient of variation 0.02) with a reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with PR about 150 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT 354 ms with RR 866 ms -> QTc 380 ms. The frontal plane is markedly abnormal: the net QRS is negative in lead I (-8.5 mV*ms), aVL and II and only slightly negative in aVF, giving a computed frontal QRS axis of about -173, i.e. an extreme (right superior) axis. The P wave and T wave are also inverted in leads I and II while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression with a tall V6 R and deep V1/V2 S waves, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation - the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with a low-amplitude upright P wave in II/I; PR about 150 ms, QRS 92 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT 489 ms with RR 858 ms -> Bazett QTc 528 ms. Frontal QRS axis +38 (normal); no bundle branch block. Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with upright P waves in II (0.19 mV, P axis about +56); PR about 180 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 378 ms with RR 1136 ms -> QTc 355 ms. Frontal QRS axis -7 (normal). Sinus rhythm, 68/min, regular, upright P in II (0.16 mV), P axis about +76, PR 135 ms, QRS 84 ms. Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. The ventricular response is fast but strikingly regular at 141/min (RR 0.404-0.456 s, coefficient of variation 0.02), and there is no sinus P wave; instead the baseline shows continuous regular atrial deflections at about 280/min - two per QRS cycle, one buried in the ST-T segment (negative trough in II/aVF about 130 ms before the QRS) and one immediately pre-QRS - giving the characteristic sawtooth appearance. No true PR interval is measurable. QRS 76 ms, QT 275 ms with RR 426 ms -> QTc 422 ms. Frontal QRS axis +2 (normal); no bundle branch block, and no paced complexes are seen despite the coded cardiac pacemaker. The previous ECG of 2022-07-11 (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation - grossly irregular RR 0.38-0.82 s, coefficient of variation 0.24, no organised atrial activity - at a mean 110/min with QRS 76 ms and QTc 433 ms. Atrial fibrillation has therefore been replaced by new atrial flutter; the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 82/min, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with a broad upright P wave in II/I and a deep negative terminal P component in V1 suggesting left atrial enlargement; PR about 185 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 375 ms with RR 728 ms -> QTc 440 ms. RR variability is increased (coefficient of variation 0.20) because of interpolated wide premature ventricular complexes, but 78% of cycles are within 10% of the median and organised P waves are present, so this is sinus rhythm with ventricular ectopy, not atrial fibrillation. QRS 90 ms, QT 371 ms with RR 976 ms -> QTc 375 ms. Frontal QRS axis about -30 (borderline normal/left). No bundle branch block. Regular rhythm at 69/min (RR coefficient of variation 0.02) with a reproducible atrial wave beginning about 150 ms before each QRS, so this is sinus rhythm with PR about 150 ms. Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction.
